daily.title: Massive Gen Z protests sweep cities across Germany
daily.summary: Young people in Germany have taken to the streets in some 34 cities, calling for greater political say and a more hopeful future. The protests come amid a wave of youth demonstrations across Europe. DW has more.

daily.title: Ukraine news: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reach Kyiv-controlled territory
daily.summary: After Melania Trump reportedly brokered a localized truce, residents of Ukraine's Oleshky managed to leave the occupied city. Meanwhile, Kyiv claimed a hit on a Russian rocket fuel plant. DW has more.

daily.title: Germany news: Merkel calls for first female president
daily.summary: Former Chancellor Angela Merkel says it's time to consider a woman as Germany's next president. Meanwhile, Berlin's Left Party is deciding whether to enter coalition talks. DW has more.

daily.title: Bollywood and the underworld — together in the spotlight?
daily.summary: A wave of shootings and extortion threats has rattled India's film industry. This time, those claiming responsibility are very different from the Mumbai underworld that had Bollywood in its grip back in the 1990s.

daily.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
daily.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

daily.title: India news: Amit Shah challenges Rahul Gandhi to debate vote theft in parliament
daily.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah has challenged Rahul Gandhi to debate electoral irregularity allegations in parliament, ahead of a major opposition rally against the election chief in Delhi.

daily.title: UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara to expire amid US, Russia vetoes
daily.summary: The mandate of the UN peacekeeping force in Western Sahara will expire on October 31. The UN Security Council could not agree on a resolution to extend the mission.

daily.title: European diplomats shun Russia at G20 gathering in the US
daily.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov declined to comment on Russia's participation in the G20 summit in December, telling DW that Volodymyr Zelenskyy should travel to Russia if he wanted talks with Vladimir Putin.

daily.title: Poland: Protesters, police clash amid top court standoff
daily.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk defended the suspension of top court President Bogdan Swieczkowski as a move to "restore the rule of law."

daily.title: Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
daily.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

daily.title: Ukraine: Oleshky residents evacuate war-ravaged city
daily.summary: Under the local ceasefire, an aid convoy of 25 buses arrived with humanitarian aid and as transport for fleeing Oleshky residents. The Ukrainian city has been occupied by Russia since 2022 and faces food shortages.

daily.title: Smuggling, power, profit: Irregular migration out of eastern Libya
daily.summary: There is currently more irregular migration between eastern Libya and Crete, Greece. It's raising questions as to what connects people smugglers with powerful militias in eastern Libya and then in turn, Europeans.

weekly.title: Tennessee woman Christa Pike describes pain after failed execution
weekly.summary: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain a month after surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee. Her lawyers want her death sentence reduced to life, while the state governor has ordered an investigation.

weekly.title: What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
weekly.summary: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?

weekly.title: US midterms: Pope Leo XIV casts vote by mail
weekly.summary: As a US citizen, Pope Leo XIV is eligible to vote in US elections and has made use of that right with a postal ballot ahead of Tuesday's midterms. The pontiff, a Chicago native, did not reveal who he voted for.

weekly.title: Binance crypto exchange suspends trades over North Korea-linked hack
weekly.summary: Crypto platform Binance has suspended trading following a suspected hack now linked to North Korea. The disruption has left users unable to trade on the cryptocurrency platform while the suspected breach is investigated.

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
weekly.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.

weekly.title: Seoul fears being sidelined as US reaches out to North Korea
weekly.summary: With ties between South Korea and the Trump administration strained, the South Korean government worries that Donald Trump's pursuit of a diplomatic breakthrough with Kim Jong Un may come at Seoul's expense.

weekly.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
weekly.summary: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

weekly.title: Italy: Students and workers rally over living costs
weekly.summary: Students and workers have marched across Italy for more school funding and relief from rising living costs. The rallies follow weeks of school occupations and protests against higher military spending.

weekly.title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
weekly.summary: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

weekly.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
weekly.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

weekly.title: Many Turkish 'guest workers' hit by poverty in old age
weekly.summary: West Germany and Turkey signed an agreement allowing the temporary recruitment of workers on October 30, 1961. Sixty-five years on, many so-called 'guest workers' can't live from their pensions.

weekly.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
weekly.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

weekly.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
weekly.summary: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.

weekly.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
weekly.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

weekly.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
weekly.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

weekly.title: Germany seeks new head of state
weekly.summary: The question of who should become Germany's new presiden is becoming pressing. Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.

weekly.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
weekly.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

weekly.title: Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?
weekly.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

weekly.title: Germany news: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses North Korea of threatening Europe's freedom
weekly.summary: Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said North Korea is putting Europe's security at risk by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in Ukraine. DW has more.

weekly.title: European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
weekly.summary: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

weekly.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
weekly.summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

weekly.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
weekly.summary: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

weekly.title: Gen Z protests in Germany: Is France-style violence looming?
weekly.summary: Young people in Germany are preparing to protest over education and climate change. Politicians fear violence like in France, but an expert sees differences.

weekly.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
weekly.summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

weekly.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
weekly.summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

weekly.title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
weekly.summary: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

weekly.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
weekly.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

weekly.title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
weekly.summary: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

weekly.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
weekly.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

weekly.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
weekly.summary: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

weekly.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
weekly.summary: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

weekly.title: What Germany thinks of carmaker Audi's $4 billion deal with Trump
weekly.summary: The luxury carmaker is set to open its first factory in the United States — a move Trump credits to his tariffs. DW examines the German reaction amid a massive auto industry cull at home.

weekly.title: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
weekly.summary: President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region but also wants good ties with Beijing.

weekly.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
weekly.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But ahead of the US midterm elections, does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

weekly.title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
weekly.summary: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

weekly.title: Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
weekly.summary: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

weekly.title: In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
weekly.summary: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

developing.title: Live: Fresh protests hit France amid heightened security
developing.summary: Police and elite security forces are out in force in French cities as thousands participate in a new round of protests. The protest location was changed last minute in Paris. Follow DW.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
